change_log.old_code: The file main.py did not exist, so there was no greeting functionality.
change_log.new_code: main.py now contains three lines: it prompts the user with input("What is your name? "), stores the response in variable name, prints "Hello,", name, "!", and then prints the fixed string "hello azer".
change_log.impact: Users running main.py will be asked for their name and receive a personalized greeting followed by the constant message "hello azer". This introduces interactive I/O where none existed before; no breaking changes or migrations are needed.

post_review.title: Missing __name__ guard leads to execution on import
post_review.body: The code runs at module level, so importing main.py elsewhere will trigger the input prompt and print statements, causing unintended side effects. This breaks typical Python module usage and can interfere with testing or reuse.

post_review.title: Unhandled EOFError when input stream is closed
post_review.body: If stdin is closed or redirected from an empty source, input() raises EOFError, causing the program to crash ungracefully. Adding a try-except block or checking for EOF would improve robustness.

post_review_verdict: The new code is very simple but lacks basic Python best practices: it executes on import and does not handle common input errors. Before merging, it should be refactored into a main() function protected by an if __name__ == "__main__": guard and include basic error handling for EOFError (and optionally KeyboardInterrupt). Without these changes, the module is not safe for reuse or automated environments.

bug_findings.title: Side effects on import
bug_findings.detail: The module executes input() and print() statements at import time, causing side effects that break library usage and can hang automated processes.

bug_findings.title: Unhandled EOFError/KeyboardInterrupt from input
bug_findings.detail: When stdin is closed or the user sends an interrupt, `input()` raises EOFError or KeyboardInterrupt, causing the program to crash with a traceback.
bug_findings.fix: Wrap the input call in a try/except block catching EOFError and KeyboardInterrupt and exit gracefully (or provide a default).
